pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/__tests__/lib/level-design/procgen-grid-export.test.ts:221 The grid export's real reader is scripts/ue/procgen_replay.py, which has a --dry-run mode that runs outside Unreal, yet the suite only regex-matches that script's source and round-trips through a TypeScript importer no production code calls, so the reader's acceptance of the artifact is never tested.

techniques.evidence: src/__tests__/lib/level-design/procgen-grid-export.test.ts:221 The artifact's reader is a Python script whose load_export and --dry-run path need no Unreal, and Python 3.12.1 is on this machine. The contract is asserted by regex over the reader's text instead of running it at unit cost.

src/__tests__/lib/level-design/procgen-grid-export.test.ts:114 The round trip runs through importProcgenGrid, which a search of src finds defined but never called outside tests. The shipped consumer is Python's load_export, so the composed path is one production does not contain.

scripts/ue/procgen_replay.py:60 The explanation of the source-text pin sits beside the pinned code, inside the haystack, where the technique forbids it. Test line 244 also pins the script's prose, and a pin is only admitted where the site cannot be executed, which --dry-run contradicts.
src/__tests__/lib/procgen-db.test.ts:6 The in-memory store differs from production's WAL mode, but the file drives the shipped record and read functions on one connection and makes no locking claim.
